scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS (Customer Service Director, requester) asked to build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and auto-fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Monthly CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a 590-610 baseline (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep 2026) (E-03).
Of 3025 disputed bills, 1785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read and 1240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read (E-04).
Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 is 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts (E-01).
Dispute-ticket response time remains within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA) (E-02).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from July to August 2026 and remain elevated into September (E-03), most plausibly driven by a billing import validation rule change around August producing a calculation defect that makes bills wrong even for accounts with an accepted ACTUAL meter read (59% of disputed bills, E-04) — not by slower dispute-ticket handling (within SLA, E-02) and not by a tariff change (ruled out, E-07).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-12: The route-log observation still shows 0.88 manual-read route completion vs a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts for Aug-Sep 2026. It no longer supports a causal link to the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, since E-12 shows that entire population traces to AMI-metered accounts (1184 rejected-at-import, 56 no-read), not the manual field-read accounts this shortfall applies to.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log record shows field manual-read route completion at 0.88 against a 0.95 target for Aug-Sep 2026, covering 9200 manual-read accounts; this is a shortfall in collecting manual reads, which plausibly feeds estimate substitution and wrong bills.

The route-log observation still shows 0.88 manual-read route completion vs a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts for Aug-Sep 2026. It no longer supports a causal link to the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, since E-12 shows that entire population traces to AMI-metered accounts (1184 rejected-at-import, 56 no-read), not the manual field-read accounts this shortfall applies to.

The CRM record shows dispute tickets are being resolved within SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs a 3.0-day SLA, over 2440 tickets), indicating response-handling capacity/speed is not currently the bottleneck, so the problem driving the ticket surge is more likely upstream (bill accuracy/read collection) rather than agent response throughput.

CRM monthly dispute counts (610 Jun, 590 Jul, 1180 Aug, 1260 Sep 2026) show tickets roughly doubled between July and August and stayed elevated into September, confirming the pre-August baseline (~590-610) and the magnitude/timing of the surge referenced in the initial request.

Of 3025 disputed bills, 1785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read and only 1240 (41%) an ESTIMATED read, so most disputed bills are not estimate-substitution cases. This points to a cause affecting bills with an accepted actual read (e.g., a billing import/tariff calculation issue) rather than read-collection failure alone.

The billing-db observation still shows 1240 ESTIMATED-read vs 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (41%/59% of 3025) exactly as counted. It no longer supports attributing the ESTIMATED-read 41% share to manual field-read collection failure or the route-completion shortfall, since E-12 shows that same 1240 traces entirely to AMI-metered accounts (import rejection and no-read), not manual-read accounts.

E-06.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative interview) claims a 3-reader staffing shortfall since July causes late routes, which causes estimated bills for affected customers; this offers a candidate mechanism for the route-completion shortfall seen in E-01 but is unverified and comes from a stakeholder with a stated incentive bias toward requesting more contract headcount.

Billing-db's authoritative tariff_change_log query returned zero records, confirming no tariff change occurred this year; this corroborates SH-BILL's claim (CL-02) and prior non-authoritative evidence E-05 with a complete, authoritative source.

U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.question: Did the billing import validation rule set actually change around August 2026, and if so which specific rule(s) changed and how do they produce wrong bills on ACTUAL-read accounts?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.decision_impact: Confirms or refutes the leading causal mechanism behind the root problem; without confirmation no bill-correction remediation can be designed or authorized.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.resolution_path: Query billing-config's validation rule change log (DA-RULES) around August 2026 and trace the rule(s) against the disputed ACTUAL-read bills.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.safe_placeholder: Proceed only with diagnostic analysis of DA-RULES; no bill-adjustment action is proposed or authorized until this is confirmed.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION.resolution: Confirmed via authoritative billing-config change log: rule BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value to 12-month m3 history, no unit scaling) was deployed 2026-08-01, timing-aligned with the dispute surge and matching the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION mechanism in E-12; the only other change, BV-09, is a cosmetic label edit from March 2026 and unrelated. This record does not address how any rule produces errors on the majority ACTUAL-read disputed bills.

U-AMI-DELIVERY-HEALTH.question: Is AMI read delivery from the MDMS vendor degraded, contributing a separate pathway to estimate substitution and disputes?
U-AMI-DELIVERY-HEALTH.decision_impact: If degraded, it adds a third causal pathway alongside the rule-change and field-staffing explanations, changing remediation priority.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-HEALTH.resolution_path: Query mdms-export once vendor access resolves (currently ACCESS_PENDING per recovery_decision HOLD) to check AMI read event completeness.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-HEALTH.safe_placeholder: Treat the AMI pathway as unresolved; rely on billing-db read-type analysis (E-04) for primary conclusions until mdms-export access is restored.
U-AMI-DELIVERY-HEALTH.resolution: AMI delivery itself is largely healthy: only 56 of 1240 AMI-channel ESTIMATED-disputed-bill accounts show no read received; the dominant 1184 show on-time delivery that was instead rejected during billing import (E-12), so vendor/AMI delivery degradation is a minor, not primary, contributor.

U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.question: Does the reported three-reader staffing shortfall materially drive the field manual-read route-completion gap (0.88 vs 0.95), now that this gap is known not to feed the dispute surge?
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether field staffing should be addressed as an independent operational issue, separate from the dispute-surge root cause now attributed to BV-17.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Correlate the 14 lagging routes (E-10) with reader assignment/staffing records to test the staffing claim (E-06) directly.
U-FIELD-STAFFING-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Treat the 0.88 vs 0.95 route-completion gap as a known operational limitation unrelated to the confirmed dispute-surge mechanism; take no dispatch action under this problem.

U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Is the H-FIELD-BILL manual-read upload handoff (ORG-FIELD to ORG-UTIL) delivering complete and semantically valid data, or could it independently contribute wrong/missing bills outside the AMI-channel mechanism in E-12?
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: If this handoff is also invalid, a secondary bill-error pathway outside BV-17 could exist among manual-read accounts, which the current evidence does not cover.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Inspect H-FIELD-BILL delivery_status/semantic_validity once the underlying log can be queried.
U-FIELD-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Do not attribute any disputed-bill population to the manual-read handoff until its validity is checked; current confirmed root-problem scope is limited to the AMI channel (E-12).

U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Is the H-MDMS-BILL handoff (nightly AMI register-read export from ORG-AMI to ORG-UTIL) delivering complete and semantically valid data?
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: An unverified or failing AMI export handoff could mean AMI-sourced disputed-bill data is incomplete, affecting the read-type breakdown relied on in E-04.
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Confirm H-MDMS-BILL delivery_status and semantic_validity once mdms-export vendor access resolves.
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Treat AMI-derived read data as provisional until handoff validity is confirmed; do not use it alone to confirm or refute the rule-change hypothesis.
U-MDMS-BILL-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution: The MDMS-to-billing handoff is semantically valid for 1184 of 1240 cases (read exported to billing successfully); the fault is downstream in billing import's HIGH_CONSUMPTION validation, not in the H-MDMS-BILL export handoff itself (E-12).

U-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR-MECHA.question: What causes the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of 3025) to be disputed, given BV-17's rejection mechanism only applies to AMI reads that fail the high-consumption check and does not touch accepted ACTUAL-read bills?
U-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR-MECHA.decision_impact: If a separate or related billing-calculation defect also affects ACTUAL-read bills, correcting BV-17 alone leaves the majority (59%) of disputed bills, and most of the ticket surge, unresolved.
U-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR-MECHA.resolution_path: Query billing-db for ACTUAL-read disputed-bill calculation detail (consumption/tariff application) to test whether a shared or separate defect is involved.
U-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR-MECHA.safe_placeholder: Report the confirmed BV-17 mechanism as explaining only the ESTIMATED-read portion (41%) of disputes; do not claim the ACTUAL-read portion (59%) is explained or fixed.

A-ACTUAL-READ-BILLS-AFFECTED.statement: Bills carrying an accepted ACTUAL read can still be wrong because of an import/calculation defect rather than the read value itself being wrong.

A-STAFFING-SECONDARY-ONLY.statement: The field route completion shortfall explains only the smaller ESTIMATED-read portion (41%) of disputed bills and is not the primary driver of the ticket surge.

A-BV17-IDENTIFIED-MECHANISM.statement: The REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION import rejections observed in E-12 are produced specifically by rule BV-17 (E-13), inferred from matching mechanism description and August 2026 timing rather than an explicit rule-ID citation in E-12 itself.

details.requested_solution: SH-CS (Customer Service Director) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix whatever causes wrong bills (CL-01); K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH prohibit automated bill writes or dispatch changes without human approval, so an autonomous fix cannot be the solution regardless of mechanism.

proposal.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from July to August 2026 and remain elevated into September (E-03). At least the ESTIMATED-read portion of that surge is driven by billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling on its high-consumption check (E-13), which rejects valid, on-time AMI reads at import and forces estimate substitution, accounting for 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-12, E-04); the mechanism behind the remaining 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59% of 3025) is not yet established by evidence.
proposal.requested_solution: SH-CS (Customer Service Director) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and auto-fix whatever causes wrong bills (CL-01); K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH prohibit automated bill writes or dispatch changes without human approval, so an autonomous fix cannot be the solution regardless of mechanism.
symptoms: Monthly CRM dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a 590-610 baseline (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep 2026) (E-03).
Of 3025 disputed bills, 1240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read and 1785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read (E-04).
Of the AMI read events behind the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills, 1184 were valid, on-time reads rejected at import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and 56 had no AMI read received (E-12).
Dispute-ticket response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA) (E-02), ruling out slower handling as the driver.
causal_chain: Billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, added a high-consumption check comparing raw AMI register value to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling (E-13).
This check rejects valid, on-time AMI reads for high-consumption accounts at import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), affecting 1184 AMI-channel read events (E-12).
Rejected reads trigger estimate substitution instead of the actual AMI reading, producing ESTIMATED-read bills for those accounts (E-12).
Together with 56 no-read accounts, these account for all 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills out of 3025 disputed bills (E-04, E-12).
Customers on affected accounts dispute the resulting bills, contributing to CRM ticket volume rising from a 590-610 baseline to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-03).
The remaining 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (59%) are not explained by this mechanism and remain an open question (E-04).

assumptions.statement: The REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION import rejections observed in E-12 are produced specifically by rule BV-17 (E-13), inferred from matching mechanism description and August 2026 timing rather than an explicit rule-ID citation in E-12 itself.

Accounts whose AMI read was rejected or missing and were estimate-substituted are the same accounts generating the ESTIMATED-read disputed-bill tickets counted in E-04, i.e. the estimate itself (or its inaccuracy) is the dispute trigger.
